meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'without' in everyday speech.

бывать.gloss: to happen, to be (sometimes); to visit

meanings.en: to happen, to exist, there can be
meanings.note: 3rd person бывает = there is / can be
Часто бывать где-то. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to happen, to be (sometimes); to visit', paired with 'быть'.

examples.text: У мужчины бывает не только жена.
examples.trans: A man can have more than just a wife.
That happens.

examples.text: У мужчины, мальчик, бывает не только жена. Это моя девушка.
examples.trans: A man, my boy, can have more than just a wife. She's my girlfriend.

meanings.note: + prepositional (where). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.
+ accusative (where to). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: How is it in Hungary?

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Everything's fine.

meanings.note: Drawing attention. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to see', paired with 'увидеть'.
Drawing attention. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to see', paired with 'увидеть'.

examples.trans: See?
I can see the toy car.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'war' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Read The Art of War, by Sun Tzu!

meanings.note: freedom from confinement (век воли не видать)

examples.text: У меня есть опыт и сильная воля.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('drawn in, involved').

meanings.note: давай + 1st person plural or infinitive

meanings.note: на днях = in the next few days, or the other day

meanings.note: 'дома' = at home. Common masculine noun meaning 'house; building; home' in everyday Russian.

meanings.note: Asks about the purpose. Core Russian adv meaning 'what for, why' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: Location. Core Russian adv meaning 'here' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

meanings.note: ironic: такая интересная = look at her, how convenient
ironic: такая интересная = look at her, how convenient

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'винный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('innocent').

examples.text: Больше всего от войны страдают невинные.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'nobody', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'ъяснить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to explain', paired with 'объяснять'.

examples.trans: I'll explain everything later.

оказаться.gloss: to turn out to be, find oneself

meanings.en: to turn out to be, prove to be
meanings.note: Reflexive verb. Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to turn out to be, find oneself', paired with 'оказываться'.

examples.trans: You turned out to be ungrateful.

examples.text: Он внезапно оказался в центре событий.

оказываться.gloss: to turn out to be, prove to be

meanings.en: to turn out to be, prove to be, find oneself
meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to turn out to be, prove to be', paired with 'оказаться'.

examples.trans: Simple things turn out to be important.

examples.text: Иногда простые вещи оказываются самыми важными.
examples.trans: Sometimes simple things turn out to be the most important.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'from; of' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: Handing something over. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'жалуйста').

examples.trans: I want to live like a normal person! I want a bidet, do you understand?

meanings.note: Понял? = got it?; понял = got it. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to understand', paired with 'понимать'.

examples.trans: Got it?

meanings.en: at times, sometimes, now and then

examples.text: Порой мы убеждаемся, что были правы.

meanings.note: Behave in a certain manner. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'ступать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to act, treat', paired with 'поступить'.

examples.text: Вика, так нельзя поступать со мной!

meanings.note: Сам, сама, само, сами. Core Russian pron meaning 'oneself (myself, yourself...)' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'делать'.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ражение'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'battle' in everyday Russian.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'традать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to suffer', paired with 'пострадать'.

meanings.note: At the start of a question. Core Russian part meaning 'so, then; like that' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: + infinitive or a noun. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to want', paired with 'захотеть'.
